title: Pipeline
summary: This file wires every stage together into one object, `RAGPipeline`. Adding documents runs chunking, embedding and indexing; asking a question runs translation, hybrid search on both wordings, fusion, optional re-ranking, a confidence decision in three bands, and generation with citations. A question goes in and an `Answer` comes out: the text, whether something was found, how sure it is, the cited chunks with doc and page, and the translated query if one was used.

key_ideas.explain: Instead of one yes/no threshold, the top score is compared with a floor and a "sure" line: below the floor you get "Not found in the documents", between the two you get the closest passage marked "not sure", above the sure line a normal answer. The first version used one cosine gate (0.80) and refused «هل عندنا إجازة الأمومة؟» even though the maternity passage was ranked first with 0.783. No single cut-off separates answerable from unanswerable questions, so the overlap zone is shown honestly instead of guessed.

With the re-ranker on, confidence is the cross-encoder logit of the top passage (floor -4, sure -2). Without it, it is the top cosine of e5-small (floor 0.76, sure 0.82). Each pair of numbers is calibrated for its model and corpus.
Hybrid search hands the top 10 candidates to the cross-encoder. The README reports that 10 gave the same or better quality than 20 at half the cost.
The embedder and generator are constructor arguments with sensible defaults. Tests pass a `HashingEmbedder` and run the full pipeline with no model download.

The design comment for confidence. Three bands: at or above SURE, answer; between FLOOR and SURE, answer marked "not sure"; below FLOOR, "not found". It explains why a single cut-off failed (no threshold separates answerable from off-topic questions, and the old 0.80 cosine gate refused questions whose right passage was ranked first) and how the floors were chosen: so that no answerable question in the evaluation is refused. The comment counts 48 answerable and 28 off-topic questions, while the README reports 46 and 24; either way the point is the same. It ends with a warning: a different model needs re-calibrating with `eval/calibrate_confidence.py`.

L27: `MIN_SCORE = -4.0`, the re-ranker floor. Scores are logits, so negative numbers are normal; below -4 the best passage is judged unrelated.
L28: `SURE_SCORE = -2.0`, the re-ranker "sure" line. Both can be overridden with environment variables, and `float(...)` converts the string.

L29: `MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.76`, the cosine floor when there is no re-ranker. e5 squeezes nearly every pair into roughly 0.75 to 0.90, so the useful range is narrow.
L30: `SURE_CONFIDENCE = 0.82`, the cosine "sure" line.

`RAGPipeline` is the class that ties every stage together.

The constructor and its parameters, all with defaults. `embedder` and `generator` can be injected (tests pass a `HashingEmbedder`); `rerank` and `translate` switch the two optional stages, both off by default here (the API and the Space turn them on); the four thresholds default to the module constants; `max_tokens` and `overlap_tokens` are the chunking budget, 160 and 40.

L73: a new empty `HybridIndex` built on that embedder.
L74: uses the given generator or lets `get_generator` pick from the environment. The extractive generator receives the same embedder, so its sentence vectors are in the same space as the index.
Re-ranker is `None` unless `rerank=True`. The import sits inside the `if`, so `sentence_transformers.CrossEncoder` and its model load only when re-ranking is wanted.
The same pattern for the translator: `None` unless `translate=True`, with a lazy import of `MarianTranslator`. The translation models (about 300 MB each) themselves load on the first question.

That would let one Space visitor's upload change what every other visitor sees.

`retrieve` signature. `k` is how many hits to return (5). `index` optionally targets a private index. `alt_queries` uses `None` to mean "not given, compute it here" and `()` to mean "given, and there are none". That difference lets `ask` translate once and pass the result in, since translation is the slowest step.
Docstring: hybrid search with the question and its translation, fused, then optionally re-ranked.

L124: the target index, with the same `is None` rule as in `add_pages`.
L125: computes the translation only if the caller did not pass one.
How many candidates to fetch per wording: with a re-ranker, at least `RERANK_POOL` (10), so the cross-encoder has room to promote a passage ranked 6th to 10th by hybrid search; without one, just `k`.
Runs hybrid search (dense plus BM25, fused with RRF) once per wording. `(question, *alts)` builds a tuple of the question followed by any alternatives.

With one wording, its list is used directly. With two, `fuse_hits` applies RRF again across the two lists, keyed by chunk id, so a passage found by both the Arabic and the English query rises to the top.
If the re-ranker is on, it re-scores the candidates against every wording and keeps the top `k`. Now `score` is a cross-encoder logit.
Returns at most `k` hits. Line 132 is blank.
`ask` answers one question end to end. `index` lets a Space session ask against its private index.

L134: translates once.
L135: retrieves with the question and that translation.

L136: with the re-ranker, confidence uses the re-ranker scale.
L137: records the kind and picks the logit floor (-4) and sure line (-2).
L138: confidence is the top hit's re-ranker score (hits are sorted, so `hits[0]` is the best). If there are no hits, a value below the floor guarantees a refusal.

L139: without the re-ranker, the cosine scale is used.
L140: records the kind and picks the cosine floor (0.76) and sure line (0.82).
L141: confidence is the **highest cosine** among the hits, not the first hit's, because after RRF the first hit is ordered by fused rank, not by cosine. `max(..., default=0.0)` handles an empty list. The values come from `Hit.dense`, which `fuse_hits` kept as the best over both wordings.
Extra fields shared by both return paths, built once as a dict and passed later with `**extra` (dict unpacking into keyword arguments).

Band 1, **not found**: no hits or confidence below the floor. Returns the not-found message in the question's language, `found=False`, no citations, but still the retrieved chunk ids (useful for debugging), and `sure=False`. The generator is never called, which saves an LLM call on off-topic questions such as "who won the world cup".
Above the floor, the generator writes the answer from the hits, with the translation available to the extractive scorer.

An LLM may still decide the sources do not answer the question and reply with the exact not-found sentence, as the prompt instructs. `str.startswith` with a tuple checks both languages. This is the second gate the README mentions: the model reads the passage, it does not just measure similarity.

Turns the generator's cited numbers into `Citation` records. Source `[n]` is `hits[n - 1]` because sources were numbered from 1; this works for both the LLM and the extractive generator because both number the hits the same way.

Returns the answer. `sure=found and confidence >= sure` puts it in band 3 (sure) when the score reaches the sure line, and in band 2 ("not sure", shown with the prefix "Not sure this answers it. The closest passage in the documents says:") when it is between the floor and the sure line. A "not found" reply from an LLM is never marked sure. The local variable `sure` (the threshold) and the keyword `sure=` (the `Answer` field) share a name; Python keeps them apart because one is a variable and the other an argument name.
